about: Born, Not Made, tail copy variant (23 Nov 2026): the parent prints the two segments of a new tail and puts a new arm together from four floating modules. Frame: x toward the parent's mouth, y port, z up, meters, origin on the tank floor; the parent sits 200 mm back from the quilted head simulator.

stages.name: The parent and the parts
stages.text: The parent, a hard tail with its DexArm and a quilted head, sits at the back of the tank. Four arm modules float in front of it in foam collars: base, upper arm, forearm, end effector.

stages.name: Pods on the floor
stages.text: The holder lays N's two sealed pods on the floor of the bowl, the way it lays a kit: a battery and a Raspberry Pi in one, the pump in the other.

stages.name: Print N
stages.text: The needle prints the nose segment folded flat over the pods: 18 layers, 79 mm tall, double wall with the quilt between.

stages.name: Cure
stages.text: Dragon Skin 30 cures in the gel for 16 hours.

stages.name: Birth of N
stages.text: The holder lifts the folded nose out of the gel and pushes it over the lip. Outside, air goes into the quilt and the segment opens to its printed shape.

stages.name: N wakes
stages.text: The Pi in the pod boots on its own battery. N has the pump, so the first part of the child is the part that moves: it swims clear of the mouth.

stages.name: Print F
stages.text: The needle prints the face segment: a quilted ring with the arm's seat plate printed into its floor, 18 layers, 79 mm tall.

stages.name: Cure
stages.text: Sixteen hours in the gel.

stages.name: Birth of F
stages.text: F is born the same way. It has no pump: it opens in front of the mouth and waits.

stages.name: N moves F aside
stages.text: N pushes F nose first to the port side, out of the way of the mouth.

stages.name: Module 1: base
stages.text: N noses the base to the mouth. The holder's crank, the hook it uses at a birth, reaches 25 mm past the lip, catches the loop on the collar and draws it in under water. It lies on the gel floor of the bowl, the base plate toward the mouth.

stages.name: Module 2: upper arm
stages.text: N noses the upper arm to the mouth. The holder's crank, the hook it uses at a birth, reaches 25 mm past the lip, catches the loop on the collar and draws it in under water. The upper arm drops onto the shoulder: magnets pull the last 2 mm and a spring latch clicks.

stages.name: Module 3: forearm
stages.text: N noses the forearm to the mouth. The holder's crank, the hook it uses at a birth, reaches 25 mm past the lip, catches the loop on the collar and draws it in under water. The forearm drops onto the elbow and clicks.

stages.name: Module 4: end effector
stages.text: N noses the end effector to the mouth. The holder's crank, the hook it uses at a birth, reaches 25 mm past the lip, catches the loop on the collar and draws it in under water. The end effector clicks onto the wrist. The arm is whole, folded, lying on its side in the gel.

stages.name: The folded arm
stages.text: Every joint is vertical while it lies like this, so every module went straight down onto the one before. Nothing was screwed.

stages.name: N docks to F
stages.text: N backs its open end onto F's rear cuff: magnets in the two cuffs, the same as the docking of a tail and a head. Pogo pads in the cuff carry the battery's power into F. The shell is whole, still without an arm.

stages.name: The shell docks on the mouth
stages.text: The shell swims round and brings its open face against the parent's mouth. Nine magnet pairs in F's cuff meet steel disks in the quilt round the mouth.

stages.name: Birth of the arm
stages.text: The holder lifts the folded arm off the gel floor, over the lower lip, and pushes it base first out of the mouth into F: 110 mm, until the base plate hooks the hinge bar of the seat.

stages.name: The shell backs off
stages.text: The magnets of the face cuff let go (the tilt release of the tail). N's jet draws the shell back and the hooked arm slides out after it, down onto F's floor.

stages.name: The arm stands up
stages.text: The seat's pogo pads touch the base plate: the arm has power for the first time. It presses its forearm on the floor and stands itself up about the hinge, and the seat magnets close.

stages.name: It looks
stages.text: It turns its base a little to one side and back, the first move it chooses.

stages.name: It unfolds
stages.text: The collars are shed and float up. The arm unfolds to its rest pose. The new tail is whole: N, F and an arm, and the parent kept its own.

stages.name: A tail of its own
stages.text: The new tail can dock to any head and print. Its two segments are quilted and soft where the parent's were printed hard on the H2S; its nose came out a little longer. Same principle, its own body.

notes: The tail splits where the hard tail is already printed in two on the H2S (x = -215 mm). Each half has less skin than a head (0.170 and 0.281 against 0.328 m2), so each folds into the head's own print envelope.

Each module floats in a foam collar trimmed so it floats the way it is joined and weighs 0.15 N in water: the parent's arm (500 g payload, a 2.45 N magnet) could not lift its own base in air (1.4 kg), but it can steer it in water. This is why the arm is put together under water, and why the water stands at 270 mm.
In the bowl the folded arm lies turned 33 deg so its elbow is not under the parent's own shoulder, where the DexArm cannot bend down (joint 1 does not lean back).
